entries.original: `thread_interrupt` also stops the background jobs the interrupted turn started (a bash command it ran in the background or that auto-detached), so the thread no longer wakes a minute later when that job ends and replies as if it had never been interrupted. The result names what was stopped as `background: { status: "stopped", stopped, failed }`; an engine that predates the stop answers `background: { status: "not_supported" }`. entries.original: Computer use v3: the session crate's side-effect funnel lands. Every mutating call runs the gate, writes a pre-input marker before the first OS call on every transport, performs the call, reads back and writes one audit event per side effect; a crashed call is never resent and reads `delivery_uncertain`. Audit, lock, permits, batches and artifact retention come with it, and a typed secret is audited by length only. Nothing user-visible changes yet; the existing desktop engine is untouched. ([#13367](https://github.com/code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent/pull/13367))
